newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian shares surge, buoyed by bank SKB.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian shares surge, buoyed by bank SKB.

text.p: Slovenian shares extended their spectacular winning streak on Tuesday, adding on another 3.56 percent on the back of vibrant demand for bank SKB after its one-week suspension.
Traders said market needs to consolidate gains after sharp and rapid rise before pressing on towards higher ground.
"SKB's shares were expected to jump even more, but obviously there was enough demand at prices below 60,000 tolars," said Andrej Potocnik, a trader at brokerage BPH said.
Demand for SKB soared due to the bank's plan to list its global depository receipts on the London Stock Exchange by mid- February.
* The 10-share SBI index jumped 55.81 points to 1,622.7.
* Overall six shares rose, 11 fell and one was unchanged, while seven were untraded.
* Bank SKB was the biggest gainer, jumping 20.28 percent to 59,300 tolars on volume of 5,039 shares. -- Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-125-8439
